summary: Verified the navbar-removal bug fix on /play and /daily. All seven gates re-run independently and green: app lint/typecheck/test/build, orchestrator typecheck/test, pack hygiene. Test count 803 / 91 files, 0 failures. No route-mode flips (/daily static, /play & /climb dynamic). The frozen-test edit is a pure ADD — one new `it` block, no existing assertion deleted/relaxed/inverted. The new test invokes the real FreeStackShell via renderToStaticMarkup and asserts the `<nav sticky top-0>` landmark is ABSENT on play/daily and PRESENT on leaderboard, with the tab band present on all three. Mutation-verified: removing the `!gameSection` guard makes the test go RED (navbar renders on /play). No collateral — diff is shell + test + handoff only; ClimbScene/ClimbPlayClient/DailyClimbClient and the redundancy work up to a3c8562 are untouched. Reverted build-generated next-env.d.ts churn; working tree clean at f80c8c8.

notes: Confirmed and did NOT flag the intentional tradeoff: on desktop the tab band sits ~56px higher on /play & /daily than on /climb. Product decision (navbar-less game > jitter-free tab band), not a regression.

happy-dom has no layout engine, so the tests correctly assert render-presence/absence of the nav landmark rather than actual pixel overlap; the browser-overlap proof was done by the orchestrator's Playwright pass at 393x852 and is out of scope to reproduce here.
The `!gameSection` guard restores the original pre-jitter-fix behavior; gameSection = section === 'play' || section === 'daily' (FreeStackShell.tsx:29).

learnings.insight: The navbar-removal fix is guarded by a mutation-verified test (climbFeelSurfaces.test.tsx): removing the `!gameSection` guard turns it red. Gates: 803 tests / 91 files, 0 fail; route modes unchanged (/daily static, /play & /climb dynamic).
learnings.action: Reviewer/QA can rely on the nav-landmark test as the behavioral contract. Do NOT re-file the ~56px desktop tab-band shift between /climb and /play|/daily as a bug — it is the confirmed product tradeoff.

learnings.insight: An absence assertion (expect(html).not.toMatch(landmark)) can pass vacuously if the landmark never renders at all. Verifying it means (a) confirming the landmark IS emitted by the real dependency (Navbar.tsx renders `<nav sticky top-0 z-30>`), plus a positive case on the leaderboard, and (b) a mutation that removes the guard to prove the negative assertion actually goes red.
learnings.action: For any 'element must be absent' test, always confirm the element is non-trivially producible and run a guard-removal mutation before trusting the green.
